evidence: La Rock is consistently described in hip-hop histories as the MC at Herc's parties from 1973, initially without a stage name and positioned out of the crowd's sight, so that nobody knew who was speaking. He was an original member of Herc's MC crew, the Herculoids. Held at consensus because no first-hand source is named here (Q22).

later.title: shout-outs over Herc's records at Bronx parties

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Nothing was recorded, so listen forward instead. Take any rap record and strip out the rhyme, the meter and the subject, and what is left underneath is a person naming friends in the room over somebody else's drums. That residue is what La Rock was doing, and it is the part that never went away.

explanation: Herc was the DJ, and his hands were busy, so he needed someone else to talk to the room. La Rock did it, hidden from view and at first without even a name, mostly calling out people he knew. So the MC's role started from a practical split of jobs, not an artistic plan. Rapping did not begin as poetry or as a performance. It began as one person greeting a room over a beat, and everything since is built on that. It is held at consensus because it rests on oral history: nothing from these rooms was recorded for release.
